title: FROM THE DAY THEY WERE PRESENTED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"This is the portion of the food offerings presented to the LORD that were allotted to Aaron and his sons on the day they were presented to serve the LORD as priests. On the day they were anointed, the LORD commanded that the Israelites give this to them as their perpetual share for the generations to come."'" - Lev 7:35-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God settled their provision on the day of their calling. Not later, when they had proved themselves. Not gradually, as they earned trust. On the day they were anointed, the arrangement was already in place.

Calling and provision arrived together.

That is a pattern worth trusting. God does not call people and then leave them to work out the logistics alone. When He sends, He supplies — not always comfortably, not always in advance, but reliably.

Jesus sent out the seventy-two with no purse, no bag, no sandals, and later asked them, "Did you lack anything?" "Nothing," they answered (Lk 22:35). Paul, who knew both plenty and hunger, wrote, And my God will meet all your needs according to the riches of his glory in Christ Jesus (Phil 4:19).

This is not a promise of wealth. Aaron's sons received meat and grain, not estates. But it is a promise of sufficiency.

If God has genuinely called you to something, you are not responsible for generating the resources it requires. You are responsible for obedience. He arranged the provision on the day He arranged the calling.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I hesitating over something God has called me to because I cannot see the provision?
2. Where has God already supplied in ways I failed to notice?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You provide for what You call. Give me courage to obey and trust You for what I cannot yet see. Amen.
